text:
maria: heads-up — support reports IPv6-only clients intermittently getting 502/503 from our API in eu-west-1 and ap-northeast-1. happens mostly on curl -6 and mobile ipv6 carriers. sample curl below:

maria: ```
$ curl -6 -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
* Trying 2606:..
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (2606:..):443
> GET /v1/health HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> User-Agent: curl/7.68.0
> Accept: */*
> 
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< content-type: application/json
< x-edge-region: eu-west-1
< x-request-id: 01F...
{"error":"upstream: connection reset"}
```

maria: not sure if it's LB dualstack announce or NAT64 fallbacks timing out. any quick ideas? @aj @lucas

aj: saw one incident earlier where the LB disabled AAAA health checks after a partial config push. can you paste the affected request-id?

maria: request-id 01F2A3B4C, and another 01F2A3D9E. both show x-edge-region eu-west-1 and ap-northeast-1.

lucas: paging through logs — the edge proxy returns 200 to the LB, but the LB then returns 502 to client. looks like LB tried IPv6 then fell back to IPv4 via NAT64 but the backend session expired.

lucas: quick recon: our ALB in eu-west-1 is in dualstack mode, but the target group health check is only bound to IPv4 endpoints in the ASG. we rely on NAT64 for ipv6-only clients; if NAT64 translation table is saturated, connections drop.

sre-oncall: @maria thanks for the traces. I pushed a temporary rule to prefer IPv4 for LB target resolution as a mitigation (sticky to dualstack disabled) — monitoring now. :eyes:

sre-oncall: mitigation command I ran:
```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes \n  --target-group-arn tg-xxxx \n  --attributes Key=ipv6.dns_preference,Value=ipv4_first
```

maria: saw a reduction in 502s for the next 10m, but some carriers still see failures. could be NAT64 capacity on the egress path to our private VPC endpoints.

aj: do we have metrics on NAT64 translation usage? where's the table?

lucas: cloud-provider exposes translation metrics via api/v1/nat64/metrics. current utilization spiked to 92% at 11:12 UTC which aligns with the incidents. also some translation cache evictions logged.

maria: ok — mitigation seems to be moving traffic to ipv4-first, but that's not a long-term solution. thoughts on adding explicit AAAA entries pointing to NAT64 gateways or increasing translation pool?

sre-oncall: long-term options:
- increase NAT64 pool / elastic egress ips in those regions (costy)
- ensure LB advertises AAAA only when backend supports true ipv6 (remove NAT64 as fallback)
- add a regional proxy pool that terminates v6 and speaks v4 to backend (we already have proxy infra but needs region expansion)

aj: value-add: we can add a short-lived probe that hits every edge region for both `curl -6` and `curl -4` and alert on >1% 502s. also add a telemetry tag to requests that go via NAT64 so we can breakdown by path.

lucas: I've opened an infra ticket to expand proxy pool in eu-west and ap-northeast (INFRA-3245). also adding NAT64 autoscale requests to the runbook.

deploy-bot: deploy status: changed target-group attribute ipv6.dns_preference -> ipv4_first (took effect 1762134578) :white_check_mark:

maria: thanks all. action items:
- lucas: verify NAT64 capacity and estimate cost for +50% pool (INFRA-3245)
- aj: add dual-probe healthcheck and telemetry tag (INFRA-3246)
- sre-oncall: keep ipv4-first mitigation for 1h and rollback if stable else coordinate proxy rollout

maria: if anyone sees new request-ids, drop them in this thread. I'll notify support and customers. :thumbsup:
